name: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2017.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The town of Mbanza Kongo, located on a plateau at an altitude of 570 m, was the political and spiritual capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, one of the largest constituted states in Southern Africa from the 14th to 19th centuries. The historical area grew around the royal residence, the customary court and the holy tree, as well as the royal funeral places. When the Portuguese arrived in the 15th century they added stone buildings constructed in accordance with European methods to the existing urban conurbation built in local materials. Mbanza Kongo illustrates, more than anywhere in sub-Saharan Africa, the profound changes caused by the introduction of Christianity and the arrival of the Portuguese into Central Africa.”

Mbanza Kongo is the capital of Zaire Province in north-western Angola, with 221,141 people in 2024. Wikipedia says it was the capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from its foundation, before the Portuguese arrived in 1483, until the kingdom was abolished in 1915, apart from a short abandonment during civil wars in the 17th century.
The article says it was founded by the first manikongo, Lukeni, at a junction of major trade routes. The Portuguese first reached it in 1491, after ten days' travel from the mouth of the Congo River.
It was declared a World Heritage Site in 2017.

gaps: Kongo voices and Angolan historians on the kingdom, beyond the outline in the article.
The Portuguese period, Christianity at the Kongo court and the slave trade, which the part of the article read here does not reach.
